newsitem.title: UK: LME copper bid higher after kerb, but trims gains.
newsitem.headline: LME copper bid higher after kerb, but trims gains.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) contracts extended kerb gains during Friday's evening session, with three-month copper bid at a strong $2,187 at the close.
Bids moved to $2,194 at one stage, but by 1912 GMT copper was only $1 above the kerb finish of $2,186 a tonne, which represented a bounce of $26 on the day.
Traders said Friday's steep gains seemed to confirm the metal's position above the tough $2,180 resistance level.

"We are... encouraged and with the spread remaining firm, are looking for challenges of $2,200 and then $2,227, with the technical indicators starting to turn off the lows," said traders Rudolf Wolff in their daily commentary.
Copper burst out of a year low of $2,140 in early dealings after a flurry of fund-led buying gave all metals a strong kick with prices ended firmer across the board.
The cash-threes backwardation moved out to $230/240 in evening bids from a kerb close of $225.
Aluminium was indicated at $1,626, unchanged from the kerb, although bids rose to $1,628 earlier.
